title: Review: Describing motion; Projectile motion; Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's second law; Newton's first law and equilibrium; Drag and terminal velocity; Newton's third law
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: K01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.14, D02-1#N.11, D03-1#N.2, D04-1#N.5, D11-1#N.3, K01-1#N.2, D01-1#N.12, D02-1#N.2, D03-1#N.7a, D04-1#N.4, D11-1#N.14, K01-1#N.5. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: Total length of the path: a scalar that is never negative.

items.label: Tension
items.clue: Pull of a string, rope or cable, acting along it and away from the object.

items.label: Horizontal component
items.clue: Part of the launch velocity that never changes, as no force acts that way.

items.label: Friction
items.clue: Force parallel to a surface that opposes sliding, or the tendency to slide.

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A horse pulls a cart along a level road, and both speed up from rest. A student argues: "The cart pulls back on the horse with a force equal in magnitude to the horse's pull on the cart, so these forces cancel and the cart cannot speed up." Which statement correctly identifies the flaw in the argument?

options.text: The two forces act on different objects, so they cannot cancel.
The horse pulls harder than the cart pulls back while they speed up.
The cart pulls back after the horse's pull has set it moving.
A cart cannot pull on anything, so no force acts back on the horse.

questions.stem: A small steel ball is released from rest in air and falls until it reaches terminal velocity. How does its acceleration change during this time?

options.text: It is constant but less than g, because drag is constant.
It stays equal to g, since drag only lowers the ball's speed.
It increases, since the ball moves faster and faster as it falls.
It decreases from g towards zero as the drag increases.

questions.explanation: At release the ball is at rest, so there is no drag and its acceleration is g. As it speeds up the drag grows, so the acceleration decreases, reaching zero at terminal velocity.

questions.stem: A runner moves along a straight track. Her position x is measured from a marker on the track. She starts at x = +30 m, runs to x = +70 m, then turns around and runs to x = −20 m, where she stops. What is her displacement?
A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: Block X (2.0 kg) and block Y (4.0 kg) rest on a frictionless horizontal surface, joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 24 N pulls X away from Y, and both accelerate together. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: System: a = 24 ÷ 6.0 = 4.0 m s⁻². Y alone: the only horizontal force is the tension, T = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 N.

questions.stem: A lamp hangs at rest from a cord fixed to the ceiling. The cord exerts an upward force on the lamp. Which force forms a Newton's third law pair with this force?

options.text: The gravitational force exerted on the lamp by Earth
The downward force exerted on the cord by the lamp
The upward force exerted on the cord by the ceiling
The gravitational force exerted on Earth by the lamp

questions.explanation: The cord pulls up on the lamp, so the lamp pulls down on the cord: the same contact interaction, equal in size, opposite in direction, on the other object.

questions.stem: Two paper cones have the same size and shape. A second cone is pushed inside one of them, doubling its mass without changing its outside shape. Both are dropped from a high balcony. Which statement about their terminal velocities is correct?

options.text: Both reach the same terminal velocity, as all objects in free fall have the same acceleration.
The double cone reaches a higher terminal velocity, as drag must grow to equal a weight twice as large.
The double cone reaches a lower terminal velocity, as its greater weight gives it more drag at every speed.
The double cone reaches its terminal velocity sooner, as its greater weight gives it a greater acceleration from the start.

questions.stem: An object moves along a straight line, with positive taken to the right. At one instant its velocity is −3.0 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is +2.0 m s⁻². The acceleration stays constant. Which describes the motion of the object?

options.text: Moving left and slowing down; it will then stop and stay at rest.
Moving left and speeding up, since its acceleration is positive.
Moving left and slowing down; later it will move off to the right.
Moving right and speeding up, in the direction of its acceleration.
